timeline.event: Olof Skötkonung, Sweden's first Christian king, is baptised

timeline.event: The Kalmar Union joins Sweden, Denmark and Norway under one crown
Uppsala University, Scandinavia's oldest, is founded
Danish king Christian II orders the Stockholm Bloodbath
Gustav Vasa is elected King of Sweden
The warship Vasa sinks on her maiden voyage in Stockholm
Gustavus Adolphus is killed at the Battle of Lützen
The Treaty of Roskilde makes Skåne Swedish
Peter the Great defeats Charles XII at Poltava
Anders Celsius proposes his centigrade temperature scale
King Gustav III is shot at a masked ball
Sweden loses Finland to the Russian Empire
The first Nobel Prizes are awarded
Norway peacefully leaves its union with Sweden
Ingvar Kamprad founds IKEA

ABBA win the Eurovision Song Contest with "Waterloo"
Sweden joins the European Union

places.name: Stockholm
places.clue: Spread over 14 islands, the capital is home to the Vasa Museum and the City Hall where the Nobel banquet is held.

places.name: Gothenburg
places.clue: Founded by Gustavus Adolphus in 1621, Sweden's second city is home to Volvo and the Liseberg amusement park.

places.name: Malmö
places.clue: Linked to Copenhagen by the Øresund Bridge since 2000, it hosted Eurovision in 1992, 2013 and 2024.

places.name: Uppsala
places.clue: Home to Scandinavia's oldest university, founded in 1477, where both Carl Linnaeus and Anders Celsius taught.

places.name: Kiruna
places.clue: This Lapland mining town is being moved east because its huge underground iron ore mine is undermining the old centre.

places.name: Visby
places.clue: Gotland's main town keeps a medieval ring wall about 3.4 km long from its days as a rich Hanseatic trading hub.

places.name: Kalmar Castle
places.clue: The Kalmar Union was sealed in this town in 1397; its Renaissance castle guards the strait facing the island of Öland.

places.name: Kebnekaise
places.clue: Sweden's highest mountain; melting ice on its south summit left the rocky north peak as the country's highest point.

places.name: Falun Copper Mine
places.clue: Once a supplier of much of Europe's copper, its mine waste gave Sweden the famous Falu red paint for wooden houses.

places.name: Sarek National Park
places.clue: A roadless wilderness of glaciers and peaks with almost no marked trails, part of the Laponia World Heritage Site.

places.name: High Coast
places.clue: Still rising after the Ice Age, this coast has the world's highest known post-glacial shoreline, about 286 m up.

places.name: Tanum Rock Carvings
places.clue: Thousands of Bronze Age carvings of ships, people and animals make this a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
